The quotation is about a "community right to buy" — a legal mechanism giving communities the first right of refusal when community spaces come up for sale. The specific mechanism is a pre-emption right over real property transactions, aimed at community ownership of local spaces.

The core economic content is about real estate/land transactions and property rights at the local/community level — this fits R3 (Real Estate Markets) most directly. There's also a dimension of collective decision-making and community governance (D7), and a legal/property rights dimension (K1 — property law).

The most precise fit: R3 covers real estate markets and property transactions. The community right to buy is fundamentally a rule about who gets priority in property sales — a market design intervention in real estate. Secondary: K1 (property law/rights of first refusal as a legal instrument) is substantively important here since the statement explicitly references legislation.
